chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruchirappalli (திருசிராப்பள்ளி, Trisira hill), the first fifteen: most confess bondage to courtesans who sell their arts and refuse a man without gold, one torments the poet with the tortures of Yama's servants, and a few turn inward to the mind, the guru's secret and the Reality beyond speech and yoga; the praise names Murugan as Sambandar, as the guru who took the poet publicly, and as the son of the Lord of the rock, often with Vayalur beside it.
structure_note: Courtesan songs: 547, 549, 550, 552, 553, 554, 555, 559, 560. 548 is addressed to the poet's own mind; 551 asks for love that scorns union; 556 is a litany of namo namas; 557 is an eight-line song asking for the guru's secret; 558 is a catalogue of Yama's tortures; 561 describes the Reality that reading, worship and speech cannot reach. Vayalur (வயலூர்), near Trichy, is named in many of the songs.

547.reading: The poet describes courtesans who beckon with an outstretched hand, show and hide their breasts, act out a false love and deal with a man as far as his coins go, recite the deceitful science of pleasure, cry like cuckoo and anril, rake him with nails and strike him to rouse his lust, having studied day and night how to confuse lustful men; he asks to leave his delusion over these whores and worship the lotus feet praised by Siva. The praise names Murugan as the one present everywhere, lacking nothing, the conscious form, the bliss the pure attain, distinct from the end of the thirty-six tattvas, the guardian of heaven whom Indra praised, the hero of Vayalur whose vel beat Sura while ghouls ate and danced, the lord of the gods on the hill of south Sirappalli with its golden towers.
547.nuance: காசளவு உறவாடி, 'relating to the measure of the coins', and சூளைகள, whores, make the trade explicit. The women's arts are a learned discipline (இன்ப சாஸ்த்ரம், பண்டு இராப்பகல் கற்று). The praise borrows Saiva Siddhanta: முப்பத்தாறினின் முடிவு வேறாய், beyond the end of the thirty-six tattvas. The line அங் மாய்ப்பரி சுத்தத் has lost a letter (probably அங்கமாய்).

548.reading: The poet speaks to his own mind: alas, do not trust this body, a contraption of strings, a lock Brahma made; from now on, without fear, let us belong to the vel-bearer who turned the mountain to cotton; this is our refuge, here is the peacock-rider's deed of possession, 'we come to rule you', and the holy ash he has bound on us; do not forget the cry 'Son, Kumara'. The praise names the drums and Vedas of the battle where Murugan played ball with the vel among the slain on his peacock, the child of grace of 'my father Sadasiva' who wears the moon, the serpent, the Ganga and the skeleton, and the lord who married the doe-eyed one and looks into the minds of those who say 'Sirappalli'.
548.nuance: The song is a speech to the mind (அந்தோ மனமே), not to the god. மயில்வாகனர் சீட்டு இது, 'this is the peacock-rider's deed', with வந்தாளுவம் நாம், 'we come to rule you', reads like a deed of possession, the claim of a master on his servant; that it alludes to a particular story is my guess. என்தாதை சதாசிவ, 'my father Sadasiva', makes the poet Siva's son as well. Many splits in the middle lines are uncertain.

549.reading: The poet describes lovemaking with women whose hearts melt, falling on their breasts, bathing in agil and sandal paste, nail marks like crescents, hair falling, bird cries, drooping carp eyes and sweat on the face, drinking their lips night and day, and asks whether Murugan should abandon him, a lecher, to be mocked. The praise names Vishnu of Srirangam, who grants grace to those who reach the supreme state through charya and kriya, as his uncle, and Murugan as the guru who came on the peacock with the vel that broke the mountain and took the poet as his own so that the world knew it, the one who appeared as a forehead mark to the Lord of the hill at Sirappalli.
549.nuance: மயிலினில் வந்தெனை ஆட்கொளல் சகமறியும்படி காட்டிய குருநாதா, 'the guru who showed the world that he came on the peacock and took me', is the poet's own claim to a public grace. The praise of Vishnu uses the Saiva terms சரியை and க்ரியை for the way to his heaven (பரமபதம்). உருவளர் குன்றுடையார்க்கு ஒரு திலதம் makes Murugan the ornament of Siva of the rock.

550.reading: The poet describes whores who weep and weep as if loving, entrap fools, will not speak to the lustful on a day they give no gold, are always angry, whose greed for coin has no end, whose eyes are steeped in poison, who price their breasts to anyone in the mansion streets, and asks whether his life can be saved from their works. The praise names Murugan as the supreme guide to wisdom, the vel of Vayalur who is everywhere, and as the poet-sage of Sirkazhi who at Madurai made the eight thousand Jains mount the stakes, spread the ash, made the Pandiya his servant and sang 'Siva Siva Mahadeva', the lord of the gods at Sira hill.
550.nuance: பொன்கொடா நாள் அவருடன் வாய்பேசிடாமை, not speaking on a day no gold is given, and அறுதியில் காசாசை, an endless greed for coin, put money at the centre. The Sambandar story is told in full detail (ஆலவாய், எண்ணாயிரர், கழு, செழியன், சீகாழி மாமுனி) and given to Murugan (வந்துபாடும் திருவுடையாய்).

551.reading: The poet speaks of creeper-like women whose small waists are a trap for young men's hearts, and of bowing at their feet and drinking their lips, and asks for the love that scorns such union and worships Murugan's shining golden anklets. The praise names him as the son, in Siva's love, of the Lord who dances to the drum in the hall that is the heart of unfailing devotees while the four Vedas sing in rhythm, the garlanded one of the Trisira hill.
551.nuance: கலவியை நிந்தித்து, 'scorning union', is unusually explicit: the plea is for a love that condemns the pleasure, not only escapes it. அன்பர்க்கு உளமெனும் மன்றில், 'in the hall that is the devotees' heart', moves Siva's dance from Chidambaram into the heart. The word திநட்முழ்குங் is corrupt.

552.reading: The poet speaks of the greed for money that the kin of women with mountainous breasts present as affection, demanding gems bright as the sun, coral and pearls, and calls himself a rogue glad at heart, mocked and deluded, futile, base, witless and without patience, and asks when Murugan will end his wandering after getting and eating. The praise names the twelve-armed one whose chest is embraced by the daughter of the lord of heaven and the daughter of the hunters, at Vayalur and at Sira hill where drums sound.
552.nuance: The demand comes from the woman's family (சுற்றம் பரிவென வைக்கும் பணவாசை): their greed wears the face of affection. The self-abuse is a list (துட்டன், அவத்தன், குணவீனன், அறிவிலி, பொறையிலி).

553.reading: The poet describes women who play with one man with their eyes, another with their breasts and a third with their hands, give their thoughts to one, their scorn to another and both their words to a third, and asks Murugan to end his delusion that such women have great love for him and to grant the feet that bees circle as if they were lotuses. The praise names the peacock that makes the serpent tremble, the hero of Vayalur whom the gods, devotees and sages worship, and the lord of Trisira hill, where Siva with the Goddess at his side, whom Brahma delights in, dances.
553.nuance: The six lines of ஒருவரொடு carry the charge: the deceit is a division of the body and mind among many men. The delusion confessed is the belief (மனநினையும் இந்த மருள்) that the love is real. வயலு஡ரா has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

554.reading: The poet describes women with lily mouths and nectar speech whose earring-touching eyes are arrow, spear and carp, who stand saying 'learn, look, come, join our desire for your shoulders', and money before a man so much as touches their cloth, and asks whether he must keep falling on their breasts and wander without rising. The praise strings epithets: the giver and great knower praised by the gods, rider of the peacock, lord of Vayalur, the deathless, ageless young one, the hero whose vel fought the demons of darkness, Uma's son, the god and king of the gods on the Trisira hill.
554.nuance: உடைதொடாப் பணம், money before the garment is touched, names the price. The women's invitation is corrupt in the source (ஓ஡ணர் பா஡ணர் வா஡ணர் சோணர்); with ஡ண read as ரீ it is ஓரீர் பாரீர் வாரீர், and சோணர் may stand for சேரீர். The praise is a chant of short epithets ending in ஏ (தேவே கோவே வேளே).

555.reading: The poet describes lovemaking with kohl-eyed women at length, drinking their lips, bird cries, the coral lips, embraces and blows done by the book of Kama, and asks whether he will stop sinking in the sea of passion. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, attended by Saraswati, Lakshmi, Rati, Sachi, the Krittikas and Rambha: Durga, the terrible one, Lady of the worlds, cause of all, Shakti, Parvati of the Himalaya, Rudri, the stainless, Lady of the religions, the partless, Kundali, Sivai, Gauri, Ambika, Tripura, Yamalai, who bore Murugan in love; and it ends at the Trisira hill of towered halls, where the Father of the hill worshipped him.
555.nuance: மதனூலின் படியிலே செய்து, 'doing it by the book of Kama', makes the lovemaking a learned art, as in 547. The second half is nearly all the mother's names, Shakta and Saiva titles together (குண்டலி, சமய நாயகி, நிஷ்களி). Whether திரிசிராமலை அப்பர் is Siva of the hill or the saint Appar is not certain; I read the former. மதனு஡லின் has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

556.reading: The poet confesses that he never took up the devotion that sings 'Hail, hail' to Murugan as bearer of the spear, knower of release, teacher of the tattvas, the true form of bindu and nada, the jewelled lamp, but fell like a stray bull on breasts smeared with civet, agil and camphor; he asks Murugan to come now and give his red lotus feet so that he does not leave him. The praise, mostly in Sanskrit epithets, names the fierce commander of the gods, the one of the tradition of offerings and soma sacrifice, the lord of Vayalur who holds the rosary, the teacher of the Saiva Agamas and tantras, the swami of the Father of the Sira hill, the lord of Vedic brahmins who keep great vows with darbha grass.
556.nuance: The opening namo-namas are quoted as the song the poet failed to sing (என்றுபாடும் பத்தி பூணாமலே), so the litany is both praise and confession. பட்டிமாடு, the stray bull that grazes anywhere, is his image for himself. The praise ties Murugan to Vedic and Agamic ritual (சோமாசி, சிவாகம தந்த்ர போதா, தெர்ப்பை).

557.reading: A short song: the poet asks Murugan to tell him the secret of the knowledge that makes clear that the Lord is the guru, so that he does not waver day and night, and to grant him the settled state of experience. The praise names him lord of this world and the next, of the three Tamils of verse and music, Saravanabhava, the god of the hill.
557.nuance: பதி குருவெனத் தெளி போத ரகசியம், the secret by which one knows that the Lord is the guru, is the doctrine that God comes as the teacher; அநுபூதி is direct experience. The shrine word சகசிரகிப் has probably lost a syllable (சக சிரகிரிப் பதி?).

558.reading: The poet traces a life from the womb through birth, pleasure and pain to death, and then the torments of Yama's servants: they bind the subtle body tight, beat and terrify it, roll it, pour sand and drop it in fire, grind it in an oil press, knock out the teeth, make it embrace a red-hot copper figure, tie it on thorns, poke the eyes, cut and feed its flesh, break and crush it and bind it in chains; he asks Murugan to end the suffering of Yama's blows. The praise names him the supreme guru at Seyppathi, praised by those who still the breath, shed the mind's cares and the senses' desires and walk charya, kriya and yoga, and the son of Siva, Rudra of three eyes and the axe who burned the three cities, quality and beyond quality, at Trisira hill.
558.nuance: The tortures follow the hell lists of Saiva and Puranic texts: செக்கிலரைத்து, ground in the press, எரிசெப்புருவைத் தழுவ, embracing the burning copper image. புரியட்டகம் is the eightfold subtle body that the messengers bind. Nothing is confessed here; the fear itself is the plea. அனலு஡டே has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

559.reading: The poet heaps names on courtesans: lustful for wealth, seats of play, shameless among men, women of illusion who throw their cloth over their breasts, goddesses of misfortune who make men poor, who couple even with outcastes, with crores of tricks, who fall on many, read only the books of union, who drink the demon's water, sinners without compassion, and asks whether pleasure with them is pleasure. The praise names Murugan as the teacher of the Vedas and Agamas by the guru's glance, the vel that killed the hunters crying 'ko ko', the lord of the peacock, born in the reed pond, with twelve shoulders, at the Trisira hill with its towers.
559.nuance: பொருளின் மேல் ப்ரிய காமாகாரிகள், 'women whose desire is for wealth', and மிடியர் ஆக்கு மூதேவிகள், 'misfortune-goddesses who make men poor', name money. பேய்நீர் ஊணிகள் probably means they drink liquor. க்஡ணடா பீடிகள் is corrupt; with ஡ண read as ரீ it is க்ரீடா பீடிகள், seats of sport.

560.reading: The poet speaks of women whose minds are set on seizing wealth, their musk-scented breasts, slipping cloth and loosened hair, and asks whether he will stop wandering in passion and, with a melting heart, praise Murugan's two feet. The praise names the bearer of the vel who went lovingly to the hill and married the peacock-like girl who guarded the millet, who came to Vayalur, and the little one given by the great Lord who appeared on the first day at the Trisira hill.
560.nuance: பொருள்கவர் சிந்தை அரிவையர், women with minds bent on seizing wealth, is the whole charge; the rest is the stock catalogue. முதனாளில் தெரிய இருந்த பெரியவர் may refer to a shrine legend of Siva's first appearance on the rock; I cannot identify it.

561.reading: The poet describes the Reality that cannot be seen by reading, reached by worship or spoken aloud, that cannot appear to the impure or be named even by those who love it, that maya cannot surround, far beyond the sound of bindu and nada, beyond the sky, the origin of the world; having seen it, he asks Murugan to teach him the true knowledge by which he may join yoga, and asks whether he must stay bewildered without casting off the flesh. The praise names the Kanda who, longing for the girl who guarded the millet, worshipped her golden feet, the peacock hero of Vayalur wearing the serpent, the Lord whom yogis who expel the breath through the nose say cannot be found, the swami of the Lord of Sira hill.
561.nuance: The first half is a negative description (வாசித்துக் காணொணாதது, பூசித்துக் கூடொணாதது, வாய்விட்டுப் பேசொணாதது) of the kind Saiva mystics use for the Lord. The tension within the song is worth noticing: the poet asks for yoga (யோகத்தைச் சேருமாறு) while the praise says breath-controlling yogis cannot find the Lord (நாசிக்குட் ப்ராண வாயுவை ரேசித்து ... காணொணாது); the second may mean only yoga without grace. வயலு஡ரத்தில் has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

links.note: Both make the courtesan's welcome depend on the gift in hand. The Naladiyar's women would send away even Vishnu with folded hands if he brought nothing; 550's will not speak to a man on the day he brings no gold.

Both picture the courtesan's double dealing as a body turned to more than one man at once: the Naladiyar's eel shows its head to the snake and its tail to the fish; 553 gives the eyes to one man, the breasts to another, the hands to a third.

Both show Yama's servants binding the soul with ropes and driving it into fire. Tirumular gives the punishment to those who urged killing; 558 names no sin, and lists the tortures at length only to ask Murugan to end them.

Both describe the Lord as beyond speech and conduct: Tirumular's great one is beyond speech, word and feeling (பேசா உரையுணர்வற்ற); 561's Reality cannot be read, worshipped or spoken (வாய்விட்டுப் பேசொணாதது).

source_issues: Song 547: the line அங் மாய்ப்பரி சுத்தத் has lost a letter (probably அங்கமாய்); வயலு஡ரா has ஡ for ஊ.
Song 551: திநட்முழ்குங் is corrupt and is not flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS.
Song 554: ஓ஡ணர் பா஡ணர் வா஡ணர் சோணர் is corrupt; with ஡ண for ரீ it reads ஓரீர் பாரீர் வாரீர், and சோணர் may be சேரீர்.
Song 557: சகசிரகிப் has probably lost a syllable (சகசிரகிரிப்).
Song 559: க்஡ணடா is corrupt (probably க்ரீடா, with ஡ண for ரீ).
